# Offline and Local-First

Dimension comparing Notion's cloud-first architecture with offline mode versus
Obsidian's local-first design. See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full
source details.

## Notion's Architecture: Cloud-First

Notion's primary data store is PostgreSQL on AWS, with all content stored as
blocks on Notion's servers [2][15]. The desktop app uses Electron wrapping the
web application. This is fundamentally a cloud-first architecture with offline
added retroactively.

## Notion Offline Mode

### What Works Offline [9]

- View, edit, and create pages on desktop and mobile apps
- Work with most block types
- Text edits merge automatically upon reconnection

### What Doesn't Work Offline [9]

- Embeds, forms, and buttons requiring live connections
- Sharing pages or changing permissions
- Real-time collaborative features

### Plan Differences [9]

| Plan | Offline Behavior |
|------|-----------------|
| Free | Manual: must select each page via menu → "Available offline" |
| Plus | Auto-download recent and favorited pages |
| Business | Auto-download recent and favorited pages |
| Enterprise | Auto-download recent and favorited pages |

### Database Limitation

"The first 50 rows download automatically." Additional rows must be individually
downloaded. Sub-pages within parent pages require individual marking [9].

### Per-Device Requirement

Offline access is device-specific — "must mark pages on each device
separately" [9].

## Technical Implementation

### Storage Layer

Notion evolved its SQLite caching system into a "persistent storage layer" that
guarantees page availability offline [10].

### Offline Trees

A "forest of offline page trees" handles multiple reasons a page might be
offline [10]:

- Pages toggled as "Available offline"
- Automatically downloaded recent pages
- Pages inherited from parent databases
- Favorited pages

Two core tables [10]:
- `offline_page` — one row per available offline page/database
- `offline_action` — records why each page is offline (`origin_page_id`,
  `from_page_id`, `impacted_page_id`, `type`)

Critical invariant: "pages removed only when the last reason disappears" [10].

### Sync Architecture

Push-based update distribution (not polling) [10]:
- Servers emit messages on page-specific channels when updates occur
- Clients subscribe to channels for offline pages
- Each client tracks `lastDownloadedTimestamp` per offline page
- On reconnect, timestamps compared against server's `lastUpdatedTime`,
  fetching only changed pages

### Conflict Resolution

"Most text edits merge automatically" with concurrent changes. Non-text
modifications (images, etc.) "may require manual review" [9]. Notion is
migrating to a "new CRDT data model for conflict-resolution" for rich-text
handling, though specific CRDT mechanics are not detailed [10].

## Obsidian: Local-First by Design

Obsidian stores all data as plain markdown files on the local filesystem [17].
No internet connection is required for any core feature. The vault is a folder
the user fully controls.

- **Sync:** Optional paid service (Obsidian Sync) for cross-device access
- **Offline:** Complete — all features work without connectivity
- **Data ownership:** Files belong to the user on their filesystem

For detailed Obsidian architecture, see
[obsidian-pa-integration](../../obsidian-pa-integration/).

## Data Portability

### Notion [5][11]

| Direction | Formats | Limits |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| Export | PDF, HTML, Markdown & CSV | Not round-trippable: "You can't instantly recreate your workspace" [5] |
| Import | .txt, .md, .docx, .csv, .html, .pdf, .zip | Free: 5MB; Paid: 50MB docs, 20MB PDF; ~120 imports/12h [11] |

### Obsidian

No export/import needed. Files are standard markdown — any text editor or
markdown tool can read them. Migration is a file copy operation.

## Comparison

| Dimension | Notion | Obsidian |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Default mode | Online (cloud-first) | Offline (local-first) |
| Offline added | Retroactively (2025) [10] | Native from inception |
| Offline scope | Per-page opt-in; 50 DB rows [9] | Everything |
| Sync model | Push-based, CRDT for text [10] | Obsidian Sync (paid) or third-party |
| Conflict resolution | Text: auto-merge; non-text: manual [9] | Sync plugin handles; file-level |
| Data location | Notion servers (PostgreSQL/AWS) [15] | Local filesystem |
| Internet required | For full functionality; yes | No |

## Gaps and Limitations

- Notion's offline mode launch date is referenced as August 2025 across
  multiple third-party sources but was not confirmed from an official
  release note in the fetched content
- The 50-row database offline limit [9] is from official docs but practical
  implications for large databases are unclear
- CRDT implementation details are mentioned but not specified [10]
- Extended offline behavior (30+ days without connectivity) was mentioned
  by a competitor source but not verified from Notion's own documentation
- Obsidian Sync technical details (E2E encryption, conflict handling) were
  not fetched
